title: Local denominators of integral total fractions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $Q(R)$ its localization at the nonzerodivisors [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $x\in Q(R)$ integral over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and $p$ a prime with $R_p$ a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then there are $s\notin p$ and $a\in R$ such that $sx=a$ in $Q(R)$.

source.place: Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal), reverse implication, denominator clearing in the step R_p = R[x]_p

proof.text: Map Q(R) into the fraction field K of R_p. Nonzerodivisors remain nonzero in R_p by the localization equality criterion, hence become units in K. Map the integral equation and use integral closedness to write the image of x as an element z of R_p.

Write x=a/b and z=c/t, with b regular and t outside p. Equality in K implies ta=bc in R_p, since R_p embeds in K. A multiplier u outside p clears this equality in R. Cancel the unit image of b in Q(R) to get (ut)x=uc.
